outcome_detail: More than 80 women (including former troopers, civilian employees, and women who attended the Junior Trooper Academy as minors) are suing the West Virginia State Police in consolidated litigation before Judge Kenneth Ballard in Kanawha County Circuit Court. In September 2025 the court ruled that each alleged videotaping was a separate occurrence for insurance purposes, meaning the state Board of Risk and Insurance Management's policy could pay up to $1 million per plaintiff rather than a single $1 million cap for all plaintiffs. As of November 2025 a mediator's proposal was under consideration by both sides; absent settlement, the first trial is scheduled for May 18, 2026, with additional trials set between June and September 2026. No global settlement had been reported as of late July 2026.
criminal_detail: A federal investigation into the hidden-camera allegations was reported in 2023, but no criminal charges over the recordings had been publicly reported as of July 2026. An anonymous whistleblower letter attributed placement of a camera to trooper Joseph Portaro, who died in 2016. Joseph Comer, the former trooper identified as the whistleblower and later named as a defendant in some of the civil suits, was indicted in 2023 on strangulation, domestic battery, and bond-violation charges in an unrelated domestic case and pleaded no contest to domestic battery and guilty to violating a protective order, with the strangulation charge dismissed.
incident_date_approx: Alleged recordings over roughly a decade or more, into the early 2020s; disclosed via anonymous whistleblower letters in 2022-2023
description: Dozens of lawsuits filed beginning in June 2023 allege that a hidden recording device was placed in the women's shower and locker room facilities at the West Virginia State Police Academy in Institute, secretly filming female troopers, cadets, civilian employees, and Junior Trooper Academy attendees aged 14-17. According to the complaints, four named individuals conspired to install, operate, or conceal the device, and images were stored on external drives and State Police computers and shared with others; some complaints also allege that a rape was filmed, that sexual and physical assaults occurred on academy grounds, and that employees faced retaliation for reporting misconduct. In April 2024, 72 additional lawsuits were filed, and by late 2025 more than 80 plaintiffs had sued. A court found that the State Police destroyed drives that likely contained hundreds of videos of plaintiffs. The consolidated cases were in mediation as of November 2025, with the first trials scheduled to begin May 18, 2026.
notes: Aggregate mass litigation: 80+ individual suits consolidated before one judge and reported in aggregate, so kept as ONE record with multiple_filings=true. Plaintiffs include both agency employees (internal-type claims) and civilian minors from the Junior Trooper Academy. Related to but distinct from the suits against Trooper Michael Miller in rec-30/rec-30b, which arise from the same broader 2023 WVSP scandal.

confidence_notes: Plaintiff counts vary over time (first suits June 2023; 72 new suits filed around April 2024; 'more than 80' plaintiffs per November 2025 coverage). Typed as class_action because coverage treats it as consolidated mass litigation reported in aggregate; individual suits are not separately documented in accessible coverage. The seed WTRF article and several station articles returned HTTP 403, so details were corroborated from search excerpts and companion outlets (WBOY, WDTV, WVNS carry the same nexstar story). The named officers are individuals identified in the complaints as alleged conspirators (Eldridge, Perry, Lee, Comer) plus the deceased trooper (Portaro) accused in the whistleblower letter; none has been criminally charged over the recordings per available coverage. Insurance ruling date is described as September 2025 by WV MetroNews; the exact order date was not found.
